title: Looking for a ReadMe Alternative? API Documentation and AI Agents
summary: Explore Theneo vs ReadMe for multi-format API docs, MCP servers, AI agents, automated changelogs, access controls, pricing, and migration.
body_markdown:
Choosing an API documentation platform is no longer just about publishing a clean API reference. Documentation needs to represent different API technologies, stay synchronized with specifications, support multiple access levels, and increasingly make APIs accessible to AI agents.


ReadMe offers interactive API references, developer analytics, and AI-powered tools. But if you're evaluating **ReadMe alternatives** , it's worth looking beyond the traditional documentation experience.


**Theneo brings together multi-format API documentation, configurable MCP server generation, automated changelogs, and granular documentation management.** Here's what makes it a compelling alternative to ReadMe.


## Document REST, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP, and AsyncAPI in one platform


One of the biggest differences between Theneo and ReadMe is the range of API technologies they support natively.


ReadMe's API reference is centered around OpenAPI and Swagger, with limited GraphQL functionality. Theneo supports **REST/OpenAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP/WSDL, and AsyncAPI** , along with Postman and Insomnia imports.


For organizations working with different protocols, this reduces the need to maintain separate documentation workflows or convert every API into an OpenAPI-based reference.


## Build agent-ready APIs with configurable MCP server generation


As AI coding assistants become part of development workflows, API documentation needs to do more than explain endpoints to human readers. Agents need structured operations, authentication requirements, and schemas to interact with services correctly.


Both ReadMe and Theneo support MCP and` llms.txt` , but they approach deployment differently.


**Theneo can generate a ready-to-run MCP server directly from an OpenAPI specification.** Teams can select API operations, configure authentication, choose STDIO, HTTP, or SSE transports, and define the target API environment.


ReadMe offers hosted MCP servers with endpoint controls and API execution. Theneo's additional option is generating a configurable server teams can run in their own environment. MCP server generation may require workspace enablement.


Together with Markdown exports and AI-powered documentation search, Theneo helps make documentation discoverable to developers and usable by compatible AI tools.


## Automate API documentation updates and changelogs


Keeping documentation accurate is often more difficult than creating it. API specifications change, endpoints are deprecated, and new functionality is introduced.


Theneo helps automate maintenance through specification imports, AI-assisted writing, and **automatic changelog generation based on API specification differences** . Teams can identify changes and update references while preserving existing customizations.


ReadMe supports Git workflows, AI-assisted documentation editing, and changelog drafting. Theneo's distinction is specification-driven changelog generation, listed from its free plan.


## Manage multiple documentation projects and control access


Different APIs and audiences often need different documentation structures. Public developers, integration partners, and internal teams may each require their own projects and visibility controls.


ReadMe Starter and Pro include one project. Multiple combined projects and advanced access-management capabilities are available on Enterprise.


**Theneo Business supports up to seven projects** : two public and five private, with advanced user and content access controls.


At $120 per workspace per month billed annually, Theneo Business has a lower published starting price than ReadMe Pro at $250 per month billed annually. Because the plans differ, compare their respective roles, limits, and features rather than treating them as identical packages.


## How to migrate from ReadMe to Theneo


Switching from ReadMe doesn't mean you need to recreate every API reference and guide from scratch.


Theneo supports importing OpenAPI specifications, Markdown content, and other supported API definitions. A migration should cover project organization, branding, publishing, access controls, and integrations.


Before launching, audit custom components, existing URLs, navigation, redirects, and authentication. Follow the[Theneo migration guide](https://docs.theneo.io/get-started/migrate-to-theneo) or[discuss migration assistance](https://www.theneo.io/book-demo) with the team.


## Is Theneo the best ReadMe alternative for your API documentation?


ReadMe remains a strong option for OpenAPI-focused teams that value developer-level API request history and usage analytics.


Theneo stands out when your requirements extend beyond a traditional API reference: multiple API protocols, configurable MCP server generation, automated updates from specifications, and flexible project access.


**The difference isn't simply how documentation looks. It's what you can build, automate, and make accessible through it.**
